book.aftermath.2.2.speaker: steve
book.aftermath.2.2.text: Mom called me from the boat that night. I dubbed her phone voicemail onto a cassette. Most nights I play it at three in the morning. I don’t know what I’m listening for.
book.aftermath.2.2.synthesis_text: Mom called me from the boat that night. I dubbed her phone voicemail onto a cassette. Most nights I play it at three in the morning. I don’t know what I’m listening for.
book.aftermath.2.2.previous_text: Nobody found them. That was eighteen months ago.
book.aftermath.2.2.next_text: A year ago a company called Halcyon Media bought KBWR.

c10_live.in.02.speaker: stephen
c10_live.in.02.text: Steve. I know you. Dad’s name is... Frank. It’s on my hand.
c10_live.in.02.synthesis_text: Steve. I know you. Dad’s name is... Frank. It’s on my hand.
c10_live.in.02.previous_text: I knocked over the microphone stand, caught it and kept going.
c10_live.in.02.next_text: It’s on mine too. Stay with me.

c10_live.recap.01.speaker: steve
c10_live.recap.01.text: The Veyr wind was a dub. The porch lights, field lamps, two grids, radios and three hundred and twelve human voices all answered it live.
c10_live.recap.01.synthesis_text: The Veyr wind was a dub. The porch lights, field lamps, two grids, radios and three hundred and twelve human voices all answered it live.
c10_live.recap.01.previous_text: The tape stopped. Three hundred and twelve voices came through the open channel.
c10_live.recap.01.next_text: To the Vigil’s instruments, Earth had just tested an engine that could reach the fleet in an afternoon.

c10_live.second.find.speaker: steve
c10_live.second.find.text: Reed brought the coast into the booth. Wen took the handoff. Both grids answered.
c10_live.second.find.synthesis_text: Reed brought the coast into the booth. Wen took the handoff. Both grids answered.
c10_live.second.find.next_text: Last cue. The wind on Veyr, and then the Choir. Nobody talks over them.

c10_live.second.lead.04.speaker: steve
c10_live.second.lead.04.text: Cue two. Bring me the real coast return. Then I’ll give Wen the grid.
c10_live.second.lead.04.synthesis_text: Cue two. Bring me the real coast return. Then I’ll give Wen the grid.
c10_live.second.lead.04.previous_text: Bell kept answering anyway. So Bell is only an echo inside the building.
c10_live.second.lead.04.next_text: I’m standing by. Wait for my green lamp.

c10_live.second.lead.05.speaker: wen
c10_live.second.lead.05.text: I’m standing by. Wait for my green lamp.
c10_live.second.lead.05.synthesis_text: I’m standing by. Wait for my green lamp.
c10_live.second.lead.05.previous_text: Cue two. Bring me the real coast return. Then I’ll give Wen the grid.

c10_live.third.find.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.find.text: The tape stopped. Three hundred and twelve voices came through the open channel.
c10_live.third.find.synthesis_text: The tape stopped. Three hundred and twelve voices came through the open channel.
c10_live.third.find.previous_text: For the first time in nine hundred years, the fleet stopped to listen.
c10_live.third.find.next_text: The Veyr wind was a dub. The porch lights, field lamps, two grids, radios and three hundred and twelve human voices all answered it live.

c10_live.third.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_live.third.lead.02.text: I’ll run the reel. Leave the tail on that last gust.
c10_live.third.lead.02.synthesis_text: I’ll run the reel. Leave the tail on that last gust.
c10_live.third.lead.02.previous_text: Last cue. The wind on Veyr, and then the Choir. Nobody talks over them.
c10_live.third.lead.02.next_text: Watch my lamp. When it goes dark, the channel is theirs.

c10_live.third.lead.03.speaker: wen
c10_live.third.lead.03.text: Watch my lamp. When it goes dark, the channel is theirs.
c10_live.third.lead.03.synthesis_text: Watch my lamp. When it goes dark, the channel is theirs.
c10_live.third.lead.03.previous_text: I’ll run the reel. Leave the tail on that last gust.
c10_live.third.lead.03.next_text: We are here. We have changed. Listen.

c10_report.in.05.speaker: archivist
c10_report.in.05.text: You were first bound in a cradle ship after Veyr’s sun failed. Fear was your first record.
c10_report.in.05.synthesis_text: You were first bound in a cradle ship after Veyr’s sun failed. Fear was your first record.
c10_report.in.05.previous_text: For a year I told you the engine was in a notebook, Saren. So you would keep looking, instead of telling the fleet there was nothing here to fear.
c10_report.in.05.next_text: I can still hear my mother in that ship. If you reconcile me, will I know her voice?

c10_report.in.06.speaker: saren
c10_report.in.06.text: I can still hear my mother in that ship. If you reconcile me, will I know her voice?
c10_report.in.06.synthesis_text: I can still hear my mother in that ship. If you reconcile me, will I know her voice?
c10_report.in.06.previous_text: You were first bound in a cradle ship after Veyr’s sun failed. Fear was your first record.
c10_report.in.06.next_text: You have spent three years selling bait to people you like. Tell them what you learned.

c10_station.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c10_station.ctx.03.text: Five weeks after Halcyon fired me, I sat at my old desk and stopped waiting for somebody else to take the microphone.
c10_station.ctx.03.synthesis_text: Five weeks after Halcyon fired me, I sat at my old desk and stopped waiting for somebody else to take the microphone.
c10_station.ctx.03.previous_text: Then I remembered Halcyon’s tower. Every ninth night for a year it had talked to the ship, alone.
c10_station.ctx.03.next_text: The rig is in pieces. We need another way onto their antenna.

c10_station.relay.find.speaker: steve
c10_station.relay.find.text: The official line sent back yesterday’s test signal. Cedar can repeat a test number but can’t see the field. Marsh, out past Sentinel Point, answered with a fresh wind reading. Marsh is our eyes, and Gull carries the live-show cues down the coast.
c10_station.relay.find.synthesis_text: The official line sent back yesterday’s test signal. Cedar can repeat a test number but can’t see the field. Marsh, out past Sentinel Point, answered with a fresh wind reading. Marsh is our eyes, and Gull carries the live-show cues down the coast.
c10_station.relay.find.previous_text: Understood. Sentinel Point, do you read?
c10_station.relay.find.next_text: KBWR is live again, and the tower that carried the ship’s signals for a year will carry ours: Elm into Return C.

c10_station.relay.lead.02.speaker: steve
c10_station.relay.lead.02.text: The official channel just sent back three. That’s yesterday’s test signal.
c10_station.relay.lead.02.synthesis_text: The official channel just sent back three. That’s yesterday’s test signal.
c10_station.relay.lead.02.previous_text: The club sent signal three yesterday, without me. Today I’m sending signal four. Let’s see who keeps up.
c10_station.relay.lead.02.next_text: Gull here. Cedar and Marsh both say four. Marsh says the wind just turned west out at the Point.

c10_town.in.05.speaker: agnes
c10_town.in.05.text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Shore dub from the original take.
c10_town.in.05.synthesis_text: Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Shore dub from the original take.
c10_town.in.05.previous_text: I brought something in my bucket.
c10_town.in.05.next_text: Mrs. Penhallow, I have never heard you say anything that wasn’t about bait.

c10_town.in.09.speaker: agnes
c10_town.in.09.text: On ninth nights I answered whatever shore phone rang. A few bars on the line kept my borrowed memories aligned. At the boathouse, you watched me do it.
c10_town.in.09.synthesis_text: On ninth nights I answered whatever shore phone rang. A few bars on the line kept my borrowed memories aligned. At the boathouse, you watched me do it.
c10_town.in.09.previous_text: Part of her. The part that stayed for the people.
c10_town.in.09.next_text: Veyr was our home, Steven. Our sun failed. That is the last wind that ever blew through our city.

c10_town.in.10.speaker: agnes
c10_town.in.10.text: Veyr was our home, Steven. Our sun failed. That is the last wind that ever blew through our city.
c10_town.in.10.synthesis_text: Veyr was our home, Steven. Our sun failed. That is the last wind that ever blew through our city.
c10_town.in.10.previous_text: On ninth nights I answered whatever shore phone rang. A few bars on the line kept my borrowed memories aligned. At the boathouse, you watched me do it.
c10_town.in.10.next_text: Two street captains, one spare phone and two streets of porch lights. Easy.

c10_town.lights.lead.01.speaker: nora
c10_town.lights.lead.01.text: Two street captains, one spare phone and two streets of porch lights. Easy.
c10_town.lights.lead.01.synthesis_text: Two street captains, one spare phone and two streets of porch lights. Easy.
c10_town.lights.lead.01.previous_text: Veyr was our home, Steven. Our sun failed. That is the last wind that ever blew through our city.
c10_town.lights.lead.01.next_text: Pier can see Orchard’s porch lights from the harbor. Orchard faces the hills, so they can’t see Pier at all.

c10_town.out.03.speaker: agnes
c10_town.out.03.text: I made this dub before I came ashore, Steven. Before I had hands that smelled of herring.
c10_town.out.03.synthesis_text: I made this dub before I came ashore, Steven. Before I had hands that smelled of herring.
c10_town.out.03.previous_text: Mrs. Penhallow, I have never heard you say anything that wasn’t about bait.
c10_town.out.03.next_text: You’re one of them. You’re the records officer Iris told me about.

c10_town.recap.01.speaker: steve
c10_town.recap.01.text: Mrs. Penhallow is part of the ship’s record keeper, the part that stayed ashore with us. She brought a shore dub of Veyr’s last wind in her bait bucket.
c10_town.recap.01.synthesis_text: Mrs. Penhallow is part of the ship’s record keeper, the part that stayed ashore with us. She brought a shore dub of Veyr’s last wind in her bait bucket.
c10_town.recap.01.previous_text: The shore dub of Veyr’s wind plays through to Mrs. Penhallow’s pencil mark, after the last gust. Then the Choir’s return opens, live. Home as it was, then a voice answering them now.
c10_town.recap.01.next_text: The porch lights on Pier and Orchard are waiting for my cue. Shaw has the lamps, Wen has the grid, and the Choir will answer live.

c10_town.recap.02.speaker: steve
c10_town.recap.02.text: The porch lights on Pier and Orchard are waiting for my cue. Shaw has the lamps, Wen has the grid, and the Choir will answer live.

c10_town.recap.02.previous_text: Mrs. Penhallow is part of the ship’s record keeper, the part that stayed ashore with us. She brought a shore dub of Veyr’s last wind in her bait bucket.

c1_dinner.ctx.03.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.ctx.03.text: A ring had been in my sock drawer for a year. I kept telling myself I would ask Nora after one of these dinners.
c1_dinner.ctx.03.synthesis_text: A ring had been in my sock drawer for a year. I kept telling myself I would ask Nora after one of these dinners.
c1_dinner.ctx.03.previous_text: Luis still keeps Dad’s old chair at the bar. Nobody sits in it.
c1_dinner.ctx.03.next_text: Nora’s oldest dinner rule was that nobody touched her plate. That night Carmen moved it twice, and Nora only smiled.

c1_dinner.ctx.04.speaker: steve
c1_dinner.ctx.04.text: Nora’s oldest dinner rule was that nobody touched her plate. That night Carmen moved it twice, and Nora only smiled.
c1_dinner.ctx.04.synthesis_text: Nora’s oldest dinner rule was that nobody touched her plate. That night Carmen moved it twice, and Nora only smiled.
c1_dinner.ctx.04.previous_text: A ring had been in my sock drawer for a year. I kept telling myself I would ask Nora after one of these dinners.
c1_dinner.ctx.04.next_text: Your plate is warm, Steve. Sit. I’m her mother, so you can apologize to me while you eat.

c1_escape.order.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.01.text: At 20:15 Nora was in Carmen’s photo, across the bay. Her staff credential was used in the north wing at that same minute.
c1_escape.order.01.synthesis_text: At 20:15 Nora was in Carmen’s photo, across the bay. Her staff credential was used in the north wing at that same minute.
c1_escape.order.01.previous_text: And the aquarium is across the bay. Eighteen minutes each way, even with every light green.
c1_escape.order.01.next_text: No. He does not know where the notebook is. Tonight? Understood.

c1_escape.order.find.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.find.text: Someone used Nora’s name and staff credential in the north wing while she was at her mother’s birthday, across the bay. And now Nora has locked me out on the balcony.
c1_escape.order.find.synthesis_text: Someone used Nora’s name and staff credential in the north wing while she was at her mother’s birthday, across the bay. And now Nora has locked me out on the balcony.
c1_escape.order.find.previous_text: Nora? The balcony door’s locked. From inside.
c1_escape.order.find.next_text: Mr. Bell’s gate. It’s the only way down from here.

c1_escape.order.lead.02.speaker: steve
c1_escape.order.lead.02.text: N. Reyes, Nora’s staff number, 20:30. She always said that north-wing clock runs fifteen minutes fast.
c1_escape.order.lead.02.synthesis_text: N. Reyes, Nora’s staff number, 20:30. She always said that north-wing clock runs fifteen minutes fast.
c1_escape.order.lead.02.previous_text: Something in the lining. Soaked. Aquarium letterhead... north wing?
c1_escape.order.lead.02.next_text: And the aquarium is across the bay. Eighteen minutes each way, even with every light green.

c1_escape.recap.01.speaker: steve
c1_escape.recap.01.text: My list: one good morning, played twice. A whistle Admiral won’t answer. Nora’s credential used across the bay. A phone call about a notebook. A locked door.
c1_escape.recap.01.synthesis_text: My list: one good morning, played twice. A whistle Admiral won’t answer. Nora’s credential used across the bay. A phone call about a notebook. A locked door.
c1_escape.recap.01.previous_text: She was close enough to stop me. She didn’t move.
c1_escape.recap.01.next_text: And Tomás’s tapes say the bay sings tonight.

c1_flat.in.09.speaker: steve
c1_flat.in.09.text: I kept the spare cassettes in my sock drawer. The little velvet box was still there. I took two tapes and shut the drawer.
c1_flat.in.09.synthesis_text: I kept the spare cassettes in my sock drawer. The little velvet box was still there. I took two tapes and shut the drawer.
c1_flat.in.09.previous_text: Record it two mornings running. If it lasts twelve seconds both times, the machine runs true.
c1_flat.in.09.next_text: Good morning, Bellwether! Yesterday will be sunny.

c2_aquarium.out.05.speaker: lyle_copy
c2_aquarium.out.05.text: The old intake is open. I have the service key. This way.
c2_aquarium.out.05.synthesis_text: The old intake is open. I have the service key. This way.
c2_aquarium.out.05.previous_text: Easy now, Steve. Nobody wants this to be hard.

c2_aquarium.out.06.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.out.06.previous_text: The old intake is open. I have the service key. This way.

c2_aquarium.recap.02.speaker: steve
c2_aquarium.recap.02.text: Nora was here, whistling for help. I didn’t hear her for five months.
c2_aquarium.recap.02.synthesis_text: Nora was here, whistling for help. I didn’t hear her for five months.
c2_aquarium.recap.02.previous_text: The north wing is no repair job. It’s a holding station, with cots, Nora’s real coat, and her voice on a tape from May.

c2_ship.command.lead.06.speaker: steve
c2_ship.command.lead.06.text: The tape keeps moving after the click. Blank tape, not leader. There’s room left.
c2_ship.command.lead.06.synthesis_text: [whispers] The tape keeps moving after the click. Blank tape, not leader. There’s room left.
c2_ship.command.lead.06.previous_text: Dad’s counter ticks once a second. The lamp lit at tick three. The buckle clicked at tick seven.
c2_ship.command.lead.06.next_text: Thank you, escorts. It is nearly dawn, and the town will expect you at breakfast.

c2_ship.command.lead.07.speaker: guard
c2_ship.command.lead.07.text: Thank you, escorts. It is nearly dawn, and the town will expect you at breakfast.
c2_ship.command.lead.07.synthesis_text: Thank you, escorts. It is nearly dawn, and the town will expect you at breakfast.
c2_ship.command.lead.07.direction: to Nora’s copy and the deputy, sending them back up the tunnel
c2_ship.command.lead.07.previous_text: The tape keeps moving after the click. Blank tape, not leader. There’s room left.

c2_ship.escape.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.02.text: It worked. Index sixty-one percent, and all of me is getting out of this chair.
c2_ship.escape.02.synthesis_text: It worked. Index sixty-one percent, and all of me is getting out of this chair.
c2_ship.escape.02.previous_text: Prefect, please repeat your instruction. The chair says you released it.
c2_ship.escape.02.next_text: The attendant is busy arguing with the column. Quietly, now.

c2_ship.escape.find.speaker: steve
c2_ship.escape.find.text: The Prefect’s own voice opened the chair at the notch marked sixty-one. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent; whatever it could bind would come later.
c2_ship.escape.find.synthesis_text: The Prefect’s own voice opened the chair at the notch marked sixty-one. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent; whatever it could bind would come later.
c2_ship.escape.find.previous_text: The attendant is busy arguing with the column. Quietly, now.

c2_ship.in.04.speaker: steve
c2_ship.in.04.text: Lyle unlocked the old intake and walked me down the tunnel under the bay. At the end of it there was a ship.
c2_ship.in.04.synthesis_text: Lyle unlocked the old intake and walked me down the tunnel under the bay. At the end of it there was a ship.
c2_ship.in.04.next_text: Glass corridors. Slow light. And a hum that was almost a tune.

c2_ship.in.07.speaker: guard
c2_ship.in.07.text: The memory index proceeds from the oldest records. Binding runs separately. Index sixty-one percent. You are now nineteen. Congratulations on your driving test.
c2_ship.in.07.synthesis_text: The memory index proceeds from the oldest records. Binding runs separately. Index sixty-one percent. You are now nineteen. Congratulations on your driving test.
c2_ship.in.07.previous_text: “You are the author of your own story.” This is from a human book. Is it helping?
c2_ship.in.07.next_text: This restraint is sticking. Release, please.

c2_ship.recap.02.speaker: steve
c2_ship.recap.02.text: They tried to make another me. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent. I didn’t know yet what the tank would bind from it.
c2_ship.recap.02.synthesis_text: They tried to make another me. The memory index stopped at sixty-one percent. I didn’t know yet what the tank would bind from it.
c2_ship.recap.02.previous_text: There is a ship under the bay. Nora is asleep on it, alive, with hundreds of others. At the far end of the hall, one bed lay under frost, and something too tall to be human slept in it. The guards never looked at it.
c2_ship.recap.02.next_text: And the woman with Nora’s face, who locked me out on the balcony and then let me go, had walked me to that chair herself.

c3_archive.out.11.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.11.text: At four minutes past midnight, the boathouse phone rang once. Mrs. Penhallow answered, listened without speaking, and hung up.
c3_archive.out.11.synthesis_text: At four minutes past midnight, the boathouse phone rang once. Mrs. Penhallow answered, listened without speaking, and hung up.
c3_archive.out.11.previous_text: She isn’t on anyone’s. Ninety-one years old, on a boathouse step at midnight. Counting.
c3_archive.out.11.next_text: I’m calling Adrian Rook. FBI. He owes me a favor from a kidnapping case twenty years ago.

c3_archive.out.12.speaker: calder
c3_archive.out.12.text: I’m calling Adrian Rook. FBI. He owes me a favor from a kidnapping case twenty years ago.
c3_archive.out.12.synthesis_text: I’m calling Adrian Rook. FBI. He owes me a favor from a kidnapping case twenty years ago.
c3_archive.out.12.previous_text: At four minutes past midnight, the boathouse phone rang once. Mrs. Penhallow answered, listened without speaking, and hung up.

c3_archive.out.13.speaker: steve
c3_archive.out.13.text: An hour later my flip phone buzzed. A text, from a number I didn’t know.
c3_archive.out.13.synthesis_text: An hour later my flip phone buzzed. A text, from a number I didn’t know.
c3_archive.out.13.next_text: “He remembers June. That doesn’t mean he’s Adrian.” No capitals. No apostrophes.

c3_house.crossword.lead.01.speaker: calder
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.text: You told me that chair indexes the oldest memories first. And you stopped it at sixty-one percent.
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.synthesis_text: You told me that chair indexes the oldest memories first. And you stopped it at sixty-one percent.
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.direction: after Carmen has gone, closing the door
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.previous_text: Carmen... I haven’t left this house since Monday.
c3_house.crossword.lead.01.next_text: I was at the station all morning, and Biscuit isn’t a witness. So you tell me. What could I ask you that the man at the market couldn’t answer?

c3_house.mail.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.mail.find.text: Dale had my letters bundled for June’s house at 08:04. The post office didn’t know until 08:12. The private channel log says only Lyle took June’s call at ten past six. He told Dale.
c3_house.mail.find.synthesis_text: Dale had my letters bundled for June’s house at 08:04. The post office didn’t know until 08:12. The private channel log says only Lyle took June’s call at ten past six. He told Dale.
c3_house.mail.find.previous_text: Then nobody tells Lyle where we go next. Or Dale.
c3_house.mail.find.next_text: June believes me. That makes one person.

c3_house.mail.lead.03.speaker: calder
c3_house.mail.lead.03.text: At ten past six on Monday, I used the private car-to-station handset. Lyle was the only one signed onto that channel. He answered.
c3_house.mail.lead.03.synthesis_text: At ten past six on Monday, I used the private car-to-station handset. Lyle was the only one signed onto that channel. He answered.
c3_house.mail.lead.03.previous_text: On Monday the post office told me Dale had already brought your letters here. Before I’d called them. So I asked for the paperwork.
c3_house.mail.lead.03.next_text: Dale’s bag left the post office at four minutes past eight, with your letters already bundled for my house.

c3_house.rules.find.speaker: steve
c3_house.rules.find.text: June’s list has thirty-one names, and most of them are feelings. Two have records behind them: Lyle’s sign-in book, and Walt’s May 3 ledger backed by a sworn hearing transcript. Mrs. Penhallow isn’t on it.
c3_house.rules.find.synthesis_text: June’s list has thirty-one names, and most of them are feelings. Two have records behind them: Lyle’s sign-in book, and Walt’s May 3 ledger backed by a sworn hearing transcript. Mrs. Penhallow isn’t on it.
c3_house.rules.find.previous_text: Agnes? She hasn’t changed in forty years. She still corrects my grammar.

c3_house.rules.lead.04.speaker: calder
c3_house.rules.lead.04.text: Walt moved to Washington in April. The clerk’s bound ledger puts him at her counter on May third while a sworn hearing transcript has him testifying in Washington.
c3_house.rules.lead.04.synthesis_text: Walt moved to Washington in April. The clerk’s bound ledger puts him at her counter on May third while a sworn hearing transcript has him testifying in Washington.
c3_house.rules.lead.04.previous_text: Mateo’s coaching book. Lyle missed every game last spring. From June eleventh, he signed in at every one.
c3_house.rules.lead.04.next_text: Two I could take to a judge. And if I do, what do I tell Lyle’s boys? Mateo says they’ve never been happier.

c4_safe.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c4_safe.ctx.01.text: Adrian Rook arrived two afternoons later with four agents and two black SUVs. He was everything June had promised. Calm. Kind. Thorough.
c4_safe.ctx.01.synthesis_text: Adrian Rook arrived two afternoons later with four agents and two black SUVs. He was everything June had promised. Calm. Kind. Thorough.
c4_safe.ctx.01.next_text: He drove us to a Bureau safe house in the hills above the bay. An hour from town, with nobody else for miles.

c5_shack.in.06.speaker: luis
c5_shack.in.06.text: I heard stories about the bay singing when I was a boy. I first heard it myself three years ago. Your father was the only one who asked what it sounded like.
c5_shack.in.06.synthesis_text: I heard stories about the bay singing when I was a boy. I first heard it myself three years ago. Your father was the only one who asked what it sounded like.
c5_shack.in.06.previous_text: Nora has been gone since Tuesday night. Carmen hasn’t slept. And I have known you since you were nine years old.
c5_shack.in.06.next_text: Forty-five years of kitchen-table notes. Every morning, one of them left the other one a note.

c5_station.in.01.speaker: autorick
c5_station.in.01.text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our control room!
c5_station.in.01.synthesis_text: Breaking news, folks: there’s a fella in our control room!
c5_station.in.01.previous_text: And my voice, on the station ident, still playing between the songs.
c5_station.in.01.next_text: Two fellas. Somebody else is breathing in here.

c5_station.out.06.speaker: stephen
c5_station.out.06.text: In a glass tank, last Friday. Cold, wet, with the index at sixty-one. A very tall man gave me a crew pass, an earpiece and a job.
c5_station.out.06.synthesis_text: In a glass tank, last Friday. Cold, wet, with the index at sixty-one. A very tall man gave me a crew pass, an earpiece and a job.
c5_station.out.06.previous_text: You woke up on the ship.
c5_station.out.06.next_text: Find the man with my face. Find Mom’s notebook. Report in every single night.

c5_station.recap.02.speaker: steve
c5_station.recap.02.text: And the man with my face had a sixty-one-percent memory index, but his last stable binding ended at breakfast before the boat. Eighteen months of my life were missing.
c5_station.recap.02.synthesis_text: And the man with my face had a sixty-one-percent memory index, but his last stable binding ended at breakfast before the boat. Eighteen months of my life were missing.
c5_station.recap.02.previous_text: Mom’s notebook was in the blue sleeve, in a shorthand I can’t read. Halcyon cleared the building every ninth night so the tower could talk to the ship.
c5_station.recap.02.next_text: They disappeared eighteen months ago. I said no to the boat trip.

c5_station.stephen.03.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.03.text: The tank slate said sixty-one was the memory index, not sixty-one percent of a person. Last stable binding: breakfast in Dad’s shack.
c5_station.stephen.03.synthesis_text: The tank slate said sixty-one was the memory index, not sixty-one percent of a person. Last stable binding: breakfast in Dad’s shack.
c5_station.stephen.03.previous_text: Sixty-one percent. That’s what the attendant said. I assumed the rest was a compliment.
c5_station.stephen.03.next_text: Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.

c5_station.stephen.04.speaker: stephen
c5_station.stephen.04.text: Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.
c5_station.stephen.04.synthesis_text: Call me Stephen. One of us should sound like a grown-up.
c5_station.stephen.04.previous_text: The tank slate said sixty-one was the memory index, not sixty-one percent of a person. Last stable binding: breakfast in Dad’s shack.
c5_station.stephen.04.next_text: Sit down. There’s something you need to know.

c6_iris.recap.01.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.01.text: I came to the pier expecting a trap. Instead she gave me a test I could repeat and a warning I could check.
c6_iris.recap.01.synthesis_text: I came to the pier expecting a trap. Instead she gave me a test I could repeat and a warning I could check.
c6_iris.recap.01.previous_text: Both calls share the same eight bars of hold music, at the minute the water lit up. Copies near the bay go below; copies far away wait on hold. Saren wants Mom’s notebook, and on Wednesday he wants the President.

c6_iris.recap.02.speaker: steve
c6_iris.recap.02.previous_text: I came to the pier expecting a trap. Instead she gave me a test I could repeat and a warning I could check.
c6_iris.recap.02.next_text: And she told me about June. They scanned her at the safe house. Her copy has run the Sheriff’s office since Friday, and the real June is locked in her own cell until the ninth night.

c6_iris.takes.lead.02.speaker: iris
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.text: The first re-sync window passed while I was chasing you. I still escorted you below later, but the window had closed. The second time, I chose not to go.
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.synthesis_text: The first re-sync window passed while I was chasing you. I still escorted you below later, but the window had closed. The second time, I chose not to go.
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.previous_text: You let me go on the balcony. And on the thirtieth you stopped at the waterline and walked home. I saw you.
c6_iris.takes.lead.02.next_text: Then say something for me. Twice. “I stayed because I wanted to.”

c7_gate.out.06.speaker: steve
c7_gate.out.06.text: In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was carrying a bait bucket. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.
c7_gate.out.06.synthesis_text: In the fog between the antennas, an old woman was carrying a bait bucket. Mrs. Penhallow. Miles from her pier, again.
c7_gate.out.06.previous_text: So we watch the hatch. I’m very good at being looked at.

c8_beach.ctx.01.speaker: steve
c8_beach.ctx.01.text: Saren came alone at dawn. He set a little Newton’s cradle on the seawall and let one ball drop. He watched it instead of looking at me.
c8_beach.ctx.01.synthesis_text: Saren came alone at dawn. He set a little Newton’s cradle on the seawall and let one ball drop. He watched it instead of looking at me.
c8_beach.ctx.01.next_text: Give me the notebook. Helen and Frank will walk out of the sea tomorrow morning.

c8_beach.second.find.speaker: steve
c8_beach.second.find.text: Saren’s message is Mom’s voicemail, cut and stitched: the same breath before ‘kiddo’, and a gap where ‘The bay is singing’ used to be. He has no message from her. He has the personal copy Rook made while he held my cassette.
c8_beach.second.find.synthesis_text: Saren’s message is Mom’s voicemail, cut and stitched: the same breath before ‘kiddo’, and a gap where ‘The bay is singing’ used to be. He has no message from her. He has the personal copy Rook made while he held my cassette.
c8_beach.second.find.previous_text: Rook kept this tape for an hour at the safe house. Long enough to copy it.
c8_beach.second.find.next_text: That’s my voicemail. You cut my mother out of her own message. No. You don’t get to trade the whole town for my family.

c8_lab.notebook.find.speaker: steve
c8_lab.notebook.find.text: America staged its test first, and China built its own from a copy, missing beat and all. Both announced themselves with the same public handshake and went out over open radio, so something out there recorded them. Mom heard that missing beat again in the bay. The fleet came because of a show.
c8_lab.notebook.find.synthesis_text: America staged its test first, and China built its own from a copy, missing beat and all. Both announced themselves with the same public handshake and went out over open radio, so something out there recorded them. Mom heard that missing beat again in the bay. The fleet came because of a show.
c8_lab.notebook.find.previous_text: Heard this before. Mom heard that missing beat in the bay. In Dad’s reels.
c8_lab.notebook.find.next_text: Film log’s on the clipboard. Tell me what you see.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.text: Both teams began with the same open-radio handshake. It told every listener when the performance started.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.synthesis_text: Both teams began with the same open-radio handshake. It told every listener when the performance started.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.previous_text: This one is our test. Before we built it, we were sent a copy of the American test to study.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.04.next_text: Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.text: Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.synthesis_text: Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.previous_text: Both teams began with the same open-radio handshake. It told every listener when the performance started.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.05.next_text: And the minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests. Your mother was in that room.

c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.speaker: wen
c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.text: And the minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests. Your mother was in that room.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.synthesis_text: And the minutes of the meeting at one table quote both tests. Your mother was in that room.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.previous_text: Both tests went out over open radio. Anyone with a receiver could hear them.
c8_lab.notebook.lead.06.next_text: They heard the demonstrations nine years ago. They came here three years ago. We called them without knowing anyone was listening.

c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.speaker: wen
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.text: I walked here from the hotel. An old woman carrying a bait bucket said good morning to me in Mandarin.
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.synthesis_text: I walked here from the hotel. An old woman carrying a bait bucket said good morning to me in Mandarin.
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.previous_text: Nobody refuses a cookie from the interpreter. It was very clever of her.
c8_lab.talk.wen.2.01.next_text: In Mandarin? Out here in Bellwether?

c9_choir.in.05.speaker: steve
c9_choir.in.05.text: The chair dragged every memory past me, but it wasn’t erasing them. Across the rail, Stephen stared at his hand. Frank. Dad. His link was failing, not mine.
c9_choir.in.05.synthesis_text: The chair dragged every memory past me, but it wasn’t erasing them. Across the rail, Stephen stared at his hand. Frank. Dad. His link was failing, not mine.
c9_choir.in.05.direction: strapped into the scan chair, frightened
c9_choir.in.05.previous_text: We will finish your scan. This time there will be no interruption.

c9_gallery.recap.01.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.recap.01.text: Nora was on her feet. Iris was still herself. For the moment, that was enough.
c9_gallery.recap.01.synthesis_text: Nora was on her feet. Iris was still herself. For the moment, that was enough.
c9_gallery.recap.01.previous_text: Stephen’s pass opened the inner pad. June saw the lamp light from the deck and called it in, and Stephen went on alone to the antenna with the rig. I stayed where I promised.
c9_gallery.recap.01.next_text: Stephen took the rig toward the antenna. Then Nora led me to row nine.

c9_gallery.recap.02.speaker: steve
c9_gallery.recap.02.text: Stephen took the rig toward the antenna. Then Nora led me to row nine.
c9_gallery.recap.02.synthesis_text: Stephen took the rig toward the antenna. Then Nora led me to row nine.
c9_gallery.recap.02.previous_text: Nora was on her feet. Iris was still herself. For the moment, that was enough.

c9_wake.ctx.02.speaker: steve
c9_wake.ctx.02.text: Iris stayed with the newly awake near Nora’s bed. Pell and Biscuit held the service hatch behind us.
c9_wake.ctx.02.synthesis_text: Iris stayed with the newly awake near Nora’s bed. Pell and Biscuit held the service hatch behind us.
c9_wake.ctx.02.previous_text: Row nine. Mom and Dad, side by side, the way they always slept. I’d brought every sound I had.
c9_wake.ctx.02.next_text: We’ve kept the service route open. Tell me who to wake first.

c9_wake.frank.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.frank.find.text: Dad answered the Thursday net before he even opened his eyes.
c9_wake.frank.find.synthesis_text: Dad answered the Thursday net before he even opened his eyes.
c9_wake.frank.find.next_text: Your mother. Play her the song, kiddo. I’ll write it down for you.

c9_wake.frank.lead.03.speaker: nora
c9_wake.frank.lead.03.text: Give me the speaker. I can hold it against his ear.
c9_wake.frank.lead.03.synthesis_text: Give me the speaker. I can hold it against his ear.
c9_wake.frank.lead.03.previous_text: Nothing. He used to say a call sign is a name you can hear through static.
c9_wake.frank.lead.03.next_text: Listen for the Morse. The Thursday club calling him in.

c9_wake.frank.lead.04.speaker: steve
c9_wake.frank.lead.04.text: Listen for the Morse. The Thursday club calling him in.
c9_wake.frank.lead.04.synthesis_text: Listen for the Morse. The Thursday club calling him in.
c9_wake.frank.lead.04.previous_text: Give me the speaker. I can hold it against his ear.

c9_wake.helen.find.speaker: steve
c9_wake.helen.find.text: The tape ran out. Mom held the last note a little longer.
c9_wake.helen.find.synthesis_text: The tape ran out. Mom held the last note a little longer.
c9_wake.helen.find.next_text: Adrian. It’s June. Come back to work.

c9_wake.helen.lead.03.speaker: frank
c9_wake.helen.lead.03.text: Up two steps. Down past home. Then back up, and hold that last note.
c9_wake.helen.lead.03.synthesis_text: Up two steps. Down past home. Then back up, and hold that last note.
c9_wake.helen.lead.03.previous_text: That’s the song in the hum. All this time, the ship was humming Mom’s lullaby.
c9_wake.helen.lead.03.next_text: You used to sing this when I couldn’t sleep. Now I need you to wake up.

c9_wake.recap.01.speaker: steve
c9_wake.recap.01.text: Dad was shivering. I put his old cardigan around him. He found the hole in the cuff with his thumb, the way he always did.
c9_wake.recap.01.synthesis_text: Dad was shivering. I put his old cardigan around him. He found the hole in the cuff with his thumb, the way he always did.
c9_wake.recap.01.previous_text: Mrs. Penhallow’s glasses, from the middle tray. Her bed tag says she’s been asleep in here for three years. So who has been selling me bait?
c9_wake.recap.01.next_text: I’m forgetting. Prefect, they’re at the antenna. They have a rig.

epilogue.bait.find.speaker: steve
epilogue.bait.find.text: Two Mrs. Penhallows, one counter, and people are finally buying bait. The Long Patience was already gone. One Adrian Rook stayed; the other took the morning ferry to find out who he was.
epilogue.bait.find.synthesis_text: Two Mrs. Penhallows, one counter, and people are finally buying bait. The Long Patience was already gone. One Adrian Rook stayed; the other took the morning ferry to find out who he was.
epilogue.bait.find.previous_text: I’ll have to find out who that is.
epilogue.bait.find.next_text: Steve, we’re home. There is coffee. Your father has labeled the paint.

i2_nora.ctx.02.speaker: nora
i2_nora.ctx.02.text: The bed panel said Monday, November fifth. That was how I learned five months had passed.
i2_nora.ctx.02.synthesis_text: The bed panel said Monday, November fifth. That was how I learned five months had passed.
i2_nora.ctx.02.previous_text: I woke up in amber light, in a bed I didn’t choose, in a hall that went on forever.
i2_nora.ctx.02.next_text: I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.

i2_nora.ctx.03.speaker: nora
i2_nora.ctx.03.text: I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.
i2_nora.ctx.03.synthesis_text: I was frightened for about a minute. Then I did what I do at any party where nobody knows each other. I started learning names.
i2_nora.ctx.03.previous_text: The bed panel said Monday, November fifth. That was how I learned five months had passed.
i2_nora.ctx.03.next_text: I can move my hand. That’s a start.
